title: Real Leveling
paragraphs: "Well... I guess you're not wrong."
"Accompanying the Spear Hero, huh... He's the kind of guy who tramples dragons underfoot—that's actually what scares me more."
"I suppose so. He's sometimes covered in blood, after all. He seems calm on the surface, but who knows what kind of fierce battles he's fighting..."
“Should we level up Éclair and the others?”
I’ll help with anything other than training our Rival team, you know?
“That’s fine, but—”
“Listen, I’d like you to at least understand what our role is here.”
Is that the pandas’ role? Technically, we’re the bodyguards for Father, appointed by the kingdom. Are we also candidates to be his concubines?
“Even so, I think if Motoyasu-kun helps us level up for a day, Lars-chan and the others will be able to fight more efficiently, don’t you think?”
“That might be true, but… they’re already fighting just fine as it is.”
“That’s true, but… I don’t think it’d hurt to pick up the pace a bit. I’ve got a bad feeling about this…”
A bad feeling, you say? I can sort of see where you’re coming from, but we’re not so weak that a few Takt remnants running amok would make any difference.
“Exactly! Instead of leaving it to the Spear Hero, we should level up Gaelion! If we have Naofumi boost his latent potential before we fight, we’ll be more efficient!”
Éclair and the others let out sighs that seemed to show they were a bit worn out by Rival’s speech.
“Since that’s the case, let’s hold off on Motoyasu-kun helping out for a little while longer.”
“Got it! Then I’ll issue some good weapons and gear to Éclair and the others!”

Fortunately, I found some drop items that look pretty decent. They’d probably be too difficult for Zou to use, but Éclair and Panda should be able to handle them. I’ll hand out the drop equipment I obtained from defeating dragons, griffins, and the like with my spear.
“This one’s for Panda, then.”

I hand over the Griffin Claw—a weapon similar to the Griffin Edge already issued to Éclair—and the Dragon Claw, a drop weapon from a dragon. By the way, it seems there are various types of Dragon Claws. The one I just gave her is the Wind Dragon Claw, a wind-attribute claw. It also boosts Agility, so it should help speed up Panda’s movements, which tend to be a bit slow.
“Oh, thank you… Aren’t you going to give it to Filolial? It seems like it would fit her, though.”
“Filolial-sama dislikes weapons derived from dragons, so it’s unnecessary.”
It’s actually just junk that takes up space in his quiver. Since many Griffins don’t like it either, it’s unnecessary.
“Ah, I see.”
“Éclair should take this, too.”
I handed Éclair the Red Dragon Sword as a backup for the Griffin Edge. Since Éclair was my forging master in the first world, I’m sure she’ll be able to handle it.
“You sure do hand out some pretty impressive weapons so easily…”

Éclair replied while lightly swinging the Red Dragon Sword I’d given her. She’s holding it more naturally than when I gave her the Griffin Edge before. That’s surely proof that her level and skill have risen significantly.
“What about Zou?”
“…You’re just calling Elmero ‘Zou’ as is.”
“No, don’t worry about it…”
Since throwing rocks seems to be his go-to move… hmm. Besides, isn’t it too big to be practical?
“Ah, Elmero won’t mind at all.”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah. When I went hunting earlier, I got a weapon from a drop that looks usable.”
Saying that, I looked over at Zou, and there he was, holding a large iron ball attached to a chain. Wow, so items like this drop too.
“I wonder if weapons that match your party members’ styles also drop?”
“I wonder?”

I haven’t really tested that aspect much. Since I sometimes picture monster drops based on my game knowledge, I can’t rule out the possibility that the weapon drops are somewhat influenced by my own mental image. Well, it’s also an opportunity to acquire all sorts of gear, so it’s probably best not to worry about it too much.
“As for armor, I think custom-made pieces are just as good as drops.”
The craftsmen in Siltvelt would surely work around the clock to fulfill a request from Father. If we don’t pay attention to that, Zou might not be able to equip anything, don’t you think?
“That’s true. I’m using the armor Motoyasu-kun gave me, too, so if we just pick out items that look usable, it’s easy to boost our combat power.”
“That’s about it. Though having a small throwing knife would come in handy in a pinch.”
“Should we use dropped knife-type items? It might be a bit of a waste, though.”
Mercenaries aren’t picky about their weapons, are they?
“Well, let’s wrap up this break and head out again.”
“Got it!”

And so, Father and the others set off once more. By the time night fell that day, it seemed Éclair and the others had leveled up sufficiently and improved their stats. They’ve become much more capable in battle, and you can really tell that Rival has been getting significantly stronger.
“So being a Hero actually boosts the amount of EXP you gain, huh? I was surprised at first, but there’s no way we shouldn’t take advantage of this.”
“Oh, so that’s really how it is?”
“I’d say so. I sensed it myself during my journey with Lord Iwatani and the others. If Lord Rasa—who’s gotten used to hunting monsters—says so, there’s no doubt about it.”
It’s an obvious discovery, isn’t it? People were saying the same thing back in the first world.
“We’re going a little further in tomorrow, aren’t we? Otherwise, we won’t stand a chance against the efficiency that Spear Hero puts out. I want Gaelion to get stronger faster.”
“I think Gaelion-chan has already caused plenty of chaos, though.”
“Not nearly enough. If I don’t gain more power, I’m worried about what lies ahead.”
“I see… Well then, let’s do our best. We’re starting to work well together, so things are looking good.”

It’s hard to admit, but Rival really understands the situation. It just goes to show she hasn’t been tagging along on the loop for nothing. If she’s satisfied with this much, it’ll make things a lot easier for me.
“I hear Takt’s dragon was already at Level 250. I wonder how strong my current Rival is?”
"Huh? Well, since we've been working on improving our stats and stuff under Gaelion-chan's guidance, it's hard to say for sure, but right now I'm Level 80."
Hmph... Is that all you've got?
"Spear Hero, are you an idiot?"
"What do you mean!?"
“This is just the groundwork. From here on out, Gaelion and the others will begin their real leveling. Just you wait and see! The next battlefield has already been decided!”
As he says this, Rival transforms into that dragon with skin resembling that water-attribute-type, Older Sister-like figure we saw before. I can’t quite figure out what this guy is trying to say.
“Naofumi, starting tomorrow, we’re switching to leveling up at sea! In this world, you get more EXP in the ocean.”
“Huh? Is that so?”
“It is! Actually, there are ways to increase EXP on the continent too, but if we do that now, it’ll create an environment where enemies tend to get stronger, so we should avoid it.”
“I see… but underwater battles might be tough for Lars-chan and Eclair.”
“Since they’ve raised you, Gaelion will do his best there. So, Naofumi, I want you to hold onto Gaelion and stay safe.”
“Got it.”

Grrr…! Rival! He’s taking full advantage of the fact that I and Filolial-sama can’t help out. If I suggest leveling up Éclair and the others here, it’ll just leave Rival and Father alone together, so I can’t say anything! That dragon!

In the end, Father and the others held a training camp for about a week in total, and not only did Rival’s abilities improve, but those of everyone around Father also grew at a pace far faster than expected. They even carried out Class Ups through Limit Breaks. Rival even bestowed Limit Breaks on Filolial-sama and the others as if it were a favor.

Out of sheer frustration, I focused even more on training Filolial-sama and, whenever I had a spare moment, continued my research on the “Eternal Filo-chan” project. I had the feeling my Doctor was sighing whenever I came in for consultations day after day, but I suppose that was just my imagination.
“Is this appearance about right for showing to the people of the kingdom?”
“Yeah, if we’re going to match the legends they believe in over there, that’s the way to go.”

A week later, Rival said this to Father when he returned from a hunt. Over the past week, Rival has been changing his appearance constantly. It seems he consulted not only Father, Éclair, and Panda, but also the people of Siltvelt and Shieldfreeden. The story goes that he was deciding just how divine a dragon’s form should be—one that could become an object of worship.

It seems he’s made a pretty solid decision. I hear Takt’s dragon was a large, blue-toned one. To counter that, he says he’ll mix in some red tones while also incorporating white sections to give it a slightly divine feel.
“So, this is next! Naofumi, what do you think of this form?”

Eventually, Rival stopped showing the presentation-ready design… and instead showed Father a brown-and-black-striped baby dragon. The tail reminds me of his Older Sister… no, it turned out to be a hybrid of a creature modeled after his Older Sister and a dragon.
“Huh? Oh, that’s actually a really cute design.”
“It’s based on Naofumi’s favorite creature from his first world. Gaelion remembers it clearly.”
“Wow, you’re really talented.”
“By the way, I can change the color scheme too!”
Rival transformed from brown into a black-and-white panda pattern.
“Buh!”
Father burst out laughing right then and there. He slowly turned to look at the panda.
The panda was staring at Rival with a very stern expression.
“Are you making fun of me?”
“Gaelion is just showing off the tricks he can do—”
Rival, is your body made of clay or something? No… come to think of it, you used to be chocolate, didn’t you?
“Well then… it’s about time we head to Shieldfreeden. I think we’re all set.”
“Yeah, that’s right. That’s why I thought I’d ask Gaelion-chan to lend a hand.”
“Then, to show some dignity and surprise, Gaelion will take human form too!”
Saying that, Rival… cast Magic and instantly transformed, taking on the human form she’d shown before. It’s Rival in her adult form. As always, she’s adopting a look tailored to Father’s tastes!
“Well, this is about it.”
“Whoa… Gaelion-chan, you’re an adult, aren’t you?”
“Heh heh, with the Dragon Emperor’s knowledge, this is a piece of cake. I want more praise.”
“Amazing, amazing.”
Ugh…
“Sakura-chan! It’s time to go!”
“Hmm…? Naofumi…”
Sakura-chan slowly approaches Father and looks up at him. Father crouches down so he’s at the same eye level as Sakura-chan.
“What’s wrong?”
“Boo.”
Sakura-chan lets out a little grumble, looking a bit dissatisfied. But Father just gently strokes Sakura-chan’s head. If this were Filo-tan, how do you think she’d react?
“Master! Filo is way cooler than Gaelion!”

I have a feeling she’d be saying that while hopping around Father. No matter how much of an angel of love Filo-tan may be, she would never make any concessions to a dragon. When you think about it that way… it’s only natural that I can’t believe Sakura-chan and Filo-tan are the same person. It’s no wonder I didn’t notice.
“Naofumi, it’s been all Gaelion and the others lately… boo.”
“What can I do? Sakura-chan and the others hate dragons.”
“Hmph…”
“I’m sorry. I’ll definitely make it up to you.”
Father looks at me with a troubled expression as Sakura-chan protests, acting all sulky.
“Motoyasu-kun, I’m not sure you should be egging Sakura-chan on like that.”
“It’s not my fault! Sakura-chan and the others are important too, you know.”
“I suppose you’re right, but…”
“Well, Gaelion is going to be busier for a while. It’s fine to let Sakura take charge of protecting Naofumi.”
Huh? That’s a remarkably generous attitude for a Rival to have. You, on the other hand, could stay away not just for a while, but forever, for all I care.
“Boo.”
“Is that so?”
“I suppose Naofumi will stop by a few places, but Gaelion plans to tour the towns of Shieldfreeden to spread the word and gather support.”
It seems he isn’t just taking advantage of the situation to tag along. But what on earth has caused this change of heart?
